definition.ja: 桜の花・花びら・枝などを図案化した文様。桜の花弁を五枚で表すことが多く、花弁先端の切れ込みが識別の手掛かりになる表現があります。写実的な枝垂桜や花びらだけの散らし柄も含みます。
definition.en: A Japanese decorative motif depicting cherry blossoms, petals or branches. Five-petaled blossoms, sometimes with a notch at each petal tip, are one common rendering; realistic flowering branches and scattered petals are also used.

ja: 五枚の花弁で構成する桜花は代表的な図案の一つ

散り花・枝垂桜・枝付きの花など、構図に幅があります
en: Five-petaled blossoms are one common depiction
Notched petal tips often distinguish stylized sakura from round-petaled plum, but not every rendering has notches
Scattered petals, flowering branches and hanging blossoms are all possible compositions

definition.ja: 梅の花や枝を図案化した文様。丸みのある五枚の花弁を単純化した梅花、枝付きの梅、紅白の梅などが使われます。桜文様とは花弁の輪郭と枝の表現が識別の手掛かりになります。
definition.en: A Japanese motif depicting plum blossoms or flowering branches. Rounded five-petaled blossoms, plum branches, and red or white blossoms are common variants; petal contours and branch details can help distinguish it from cherry blossom motifs.

花の中心に花蕊を描く表現が見られます
桜との判別は花弁の形や枝ぶりを総合して行い、色だけでは判別しません

A visible central cluster of stamens is a useful cue in detailed examples
Color alone does not reliably distinguish plum from cherry; inspect petals and branches

五弁花の桜・梅とは花弁の数と長さが主な識別点です

Layered petals, large blossoms and leaves appear in varied designs
Numerous slender petals distinguish typical chrysanthemums from five-petaled plum or cherry

definition.en: A Japanese decorative motif representing cranes, shown flying with outstretched wings, standing, or combined with pines and waves; in Japanese textiles it often conveys auspicious longevity.

羽先を黒く描く、赤い頭頂部を示すなどの表現例がありますが固定条件ではありません
小鳥の千鳥文様とは鳥の体格や翼・脚の表現、構図が異なります
en: Long neck, legs and broad outstretched wings can signal a crane
Black wing tips or a red crown are optional illustrative features, not universal requirements
Compared with plover motifs, cranes are usually depicted with longer necks and legs

definition.ja: 丸みを帯びた六方の輪郭を用いる日本の伝統文様。雪の意匠として古くから着物や工芸に使われ、輪郭を枠として他の花草文様を配する例もあります。成立の由来には複数の説明があり、近代的な雪結晶図から直接生まれたとは断定できません。
definition.en: A traditional Japanese snow-related ornament with a rounded, broadly sixfold outline, used on garments and crafts and sometimes as a framing shape for other motifs. Its precise historical origin is debated; it should not be asserted to derive directly from modern snow-crystal diagrams.

ja: 六方の丸みを帯びた連続する輪郭が一般的な識別点です
内部に草花など別の文様を配置して枠にする場合があります
雪の結晶を示す鋭い幾何学図とは区別し、成立の由来は断定しません
en: A rounded, approximately sixfold scalloped outline is common
The shape may serve as a frame containing flowers or other designs
Distinguish traditional snow-ring from sharp geometric snowflake illustrations; origin remains debated

definition.ja: 細長い楕円状の渦や流れを組み合わせ、水の動きを示す日本の文様。観世流の謡本や能装束に関わる意匠として知られ、染織・漆工にも用いられました。一般的な波の半円反復とは異なり、横長の渦の輪郭が識別点になります。
definition.en: A Japanese water ornament built from elongated, oval swirls suggesting moving or circulating water. Associated with the Kanze school of Noh and found on performance garments, book covers and decorative arts, it differs from semicircular wave repeats through its curling, oval flow.

ja: 横長の楕円・渦巻き状の水の線が主な目印です
青海波の同心半円を並べる構成とは異なり、流線が曲がって巻き込みます

en: Look for long, curling oval/spiral lines suggesting flowing water
Unlike repeated concentric semicircles of seigaiha, the streams coil or turn
Number and spacing of spirals vary among historical works

definition.ja: 八角形や四角形の枠を幾何学的につなぎ、その内側に花・唐草などを配する文様群。名称は中国の蜀にゆかりのある錦に結びつきます。歴史資料には格子や連珠を組み合わせる異なる構成があり、すべてが一つの固定図案ではありません。
definition.en: A family of geometric brocade designs using interconnected octagonal and square compartments with floral or scrolling motifs inside. Associated with Shu (Shokko) brocades, historic examples differ in their grids, pearl roundels and internal ornament rather than sharing one immutable repeat.

ja: 八角形と四角形を組み合わせる区画構造が典型例です
区画の内部に花・唐草などの細部を入れます
ただの格子や一様な八角タイルとは異なり、装飾区画の構成が重要です
en: An octagon-and-square compartment network is one common example
Floral or scrolling ornaments appear inside the compartments
Do not reduce all historic Shokko textiles to one identical octagonal grid

definition.en: A Japanese motif formed by joining a large central diamond to smaller diamonds above and below. It may stand alone, repeat as a linked pattern, or define sections of dyed cloth. The name is traditionally associated with fissures in pine bark.

Unlike an equal-size diamond lattice or argyle, the three stacked forms differ in scale
It can be repeated or used to divide different dyed sections
